strategies.summary: Phase-1 trace shows all LN-fusing attempts failed at compile time due to python_region_syntax_error and invalid_candidate_format, not from a fundamental algorithmic problem. The remaining bottleneck after SDPA is forward_stmt_5: self.norm(attn_output + residual). This is a two-pass kernel today (elementwise add + LN reduce). Write a minimal fused CUDA kernel that takes attn_output and residual as inputs, performs the add in registers, then does a single-pass online Welford mean/variance reduction per row (sequence position), and writes the normalized output. For embed_dim=128 this fits in 4 warps with full warp-level reduction via __shfl_xor_sync.
implementation_hints: Each CUDA block handles one row (one token position): gridDim=(B*HW,), blockDim=128 threads â one thread per channel
Thread loads attn_output[i] + residual[i] into a register, accumulates mean and M2 via Welford in shared memory with a two-level warp+block reduction
After reduction, normalize in-place: out[i] = (val - mean) / sqrt(var + eps) * gamma[i] + beta[i]
gamma and beta come from self.norm.weight and self.norm.bias, passed as pointers
Export as fused_add_layernorm(attn_output, residual, weight, bias, eps) -> Tensor in cuda_cpp, call in forward_stmt_5
Avoid the python_region_syntax_error failures by keeping cuda_cpp strictly C++ with no Python syntax; previous failures were likely from embedding Python-style strings inside the C++ region
strategies.expected_gain: 5-12% reduction in total runtime by halving the memory round-trips for the add+norm sequence (saves one full (B, HW, C) read+write pass)
risk_notes: Must pass gamma and beta as separate arguments; do not bake them into the kernel as constants since they are learnable
eps must match nn.LayerNorm default (1e-5); expose as a kernel parameter
Numerical agreement: Welford online algorithm matches PyTorch's two-pass LN to within 1e-5 for float32 at dim=128

    for line in source.splitlines():
